old: A 1973 10 cents from Singapore. Value side rice stalk left, large 10, CENTS, 1973, SINGAPORE, national arms and lion-fish on the obverse. Struck in cupronickel.
new: A 1973 10 cents from Singapore. Value side two stalks of rice, large 10, CENTS, 1973, SINGAPORE; the other side shows a crowned seahorse. Struck in cupronickel.
source: Numista N#1671 (https://en.numista.com/catalogue/pieces1671.html): Singapore 10 cents 1967-1985 (KM# 3, Schön# 3): obverse 'Denomination flanked by two stalks of paddy' (lettering 1974 SINGAPORE 10 CENTS); reverse 'Crowned Seahorse (Binomial Name: Hippocampus coronatus)'; engraver Stuart Devlin; copper-nickel 75/25; 1973 row 14 290 000 (matches the record). The story said 'national arms and lion-fish on the obverse'; this coin has no arms and the lionfish is the 50-cent design, so only that sentence is changed (same error as C250, fixed in changes_grok-bot_20261008-1103.jsonl). 'rice stalk left' rewritten as the entry's two stalks.
